itinerary.cal: Most parties make this a 2-3 day backpack. Fast parties have done it car-to-car in a single long day, with reported times from under 12 hours up to about 19 hours when combined with other summits.

days.objective: Camp at Buck Creek Pass or below Pass No Pass

days.note: Climb Fortress from camp, very often combined with Buck Mountain and/or Chiwawa Mountain.
days.title: Climb Fortress Mountain
days.objective: Climb the Southwest Face and return to camp

days.note: Hike back out to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out to Trinity
days.objective: Return to the Trinity Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: Hike about 9-9.5 miles to camp at Buck Creek Pass or the basin below Pass No Pass, climb Fortress (often with Buck or Chiwawa Mountain) from camp, and hike out on the third day.

itinerary.cal: Most parties base out of the bench camp at about 6,500 ft below the spire; an alpine start is strongly recommended so the descent isn't finished in the dark.

days.note: Hike from the highway pullout to the bench camp at about 6,500 ft below the spire.
days.title: Hike to the bench camp
days.objective: Camp on the 6,500-ft bench

days.note: Make an alpine start and approach the base of the route from camp. Climb the 12 pitches (one fast party of four went camp-to-camp in 9.5 hours), then budget several hours for the slow, loose descent gully.
days.title: Climb Gato Negro
days.objective: Climb the 12 pitches and return to camp

days.note: Pack up the bench camp and hike back to the highway.
days.title: Hike out to the highway
days.objective: Return to the pullout

itinerary.totalNote: Hike to the 6,500-ft bench camp, spend a full day on the 12 pitches and the slow, loose descent gully, and hike back out.

timing.recommendedStart: Early from Perfect Pass camp — budget several hours for the roped glacier crossing to the base of the route before any technical climbing begins

itinerary.cal: Season is July to August. This is a committing three-day glacier trip with essentially no bailout once past the Imperfect Impasse.

days.note: Hike roughly 16 miles from the Hannegan Pass Trailhead via Hannegan Pass, the Chilliwack River ford, Easy Ridge and the Imperfect Impasse to camp at Perfect Pass. It is a full day with about 7,000 ft of gain.
days.title: Hike in to Perfect Pass
days.objective: Reach camp at Perfect Pass

days.note: Rope up and cross the Challenger Glacier to the base of Poltergeist Pinnacle, roughly 3 hours from camp per the first-ascent account. Climb the East Face route (3 technical pitches plus about 800 ft of simul-climbed ridge) and traverse to Mount Challenger's summit. Descend the Challenger Glacier back to camp at Perfect Pass.
days.title: Climb Poltergeist Pinnacle and Challenger
days.objective: Summit Poltergeist Pinnacle and Mount Challenger

days.note: Hike out from Perfect Pass to the trailhead, reversing the approach over Easy Ridge, the Chilliwack River and Hannegan Pass.
days.title: Hike out to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Hannegan Pass Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: Three days: a full day in to Perfect Pass, a glacier-and-rock summit day on Poltergeist Pinnacle and Mount Challenger, and a day out.

itinerary.cal: July through September, once Aasgard Pass sheds most of its snow. Overnight stays in the Enchantments need an advance lottery/permit (May 15 - Oct 15), so most parties plan three days around their permit dates.

days.note: From the Stuart Lake trailhead go to Colchuck Lake (about 4 mi, 2,300 ft), then grind up Aasgard Pass (about 2,200 ft in under a mile) to 7,800 ft and cross the Core past Isolation and Tranquil lakes to Gnome Tarn. Total is roughly 8 mi; gain uses WTA's 4,500 ft to the pass and loss is an estimate for the drop to the tarn.
days.title: Hike over Aasgard Pass to Gnome Tarn
days.objective: Reach the Gnome Tarn bivy below the south face

days.note: The 80 ft 5.10+ finger crack starts about 20 ft left of the normal Stanley-Burgner start and tops out at the same belay, so most parties link it into Stanley-Burgner P2 and continue to the summit. One party climbed Stanley-Burgner in 4.5 hours base to summit and took about an hour to rappel the north side and walk back to the base.
days.title: Climb the finger crack and Stanley-Burgner
days.objective: Climb the pitch, link into Stanley-Burgner and summit

days.note: The Snow Lakes trail is about 10 mi from the Prusik area and loses more than a mile of elevation; one party took just under 6 hours from the base of Prusik to the car. This needs a car or shuttle at the Snow Lakes trailhead; reversing Aasgard Pass is the alternative.
days.title: Hike out via the Snow Lakes
days.objective: Descend past Viviane, Snow and Nada lakes

itinerary.totalNote: A three-day Enchantments trip: over Aasgard Pass to Gnome Tarn, the one-pitch finger crack linked into Stanley-Burgner to the summit, and out the Snow Lakes trail.

sectionBreakdown.note: Follow the PCT down the upper White Chuck valley to Sitkum Creek, then take the steep, unsigned climbers' path up the ridge south of the creek to the high camp at Boulder Basin.

sectionBreakdown.note: Rope up from Boulder Basin, climb the heavily crevassed Sitkum Glacier to a saddle near Sitkum Spire (~9,500 ft), then follow the pumice/scree ridge (with one short snow traverse) …

schedule.label: Reach the ~9,500 ft saddle

itinerary.cal: Two camps are used: Silver Lake (water taxi and hike via Silver Creek) or Ouzel Lake (Depot Creek hike).

days.note: Take the water taxi and hike in to camp at Silver Lake, or hike Depot Creek to Ouzel Lake.
days.title: Hike in to Silver Lake or Ouzel Lake
days.objective: Reach camp below the Silver Glacier

days.note: From Ouzel Lake climb the gully to the Custer-Spickard saddle, or from Silver Lake cross the moraine to the glacier toe. Cross the Silver Glacier and climb the summit step (roughly 3-4 hours summit-bound from Silver Lake camp), then return to camp.
days.title: Climb the Silver Glacier
days.objective: Summit via the Silver Glacier and return to camp

days.note: Hike out and catch the water taxi, or hike out via Depot Creek.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the lake or trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: Water-taxi and hike (or hike Depot Creek) to a Silver Lake or Ouzel Lake camp, cross the Silver Glacier to climb the summit step and return to camp, then hike out.

days.note: From Gnome Tarn walk about 20 minutes to the south face and find the large right-facing dihedral about 20 yards left of Solid Gold. days.title: Climb Sail Away
days.objective: Climb six pitches to the Sail headwall and rappel

days.note: The Snow Lakes trail is about 10 mi from the Prusik area and loses more than a mile of elevation; one party took just under 6 hours from the base of Prusik to the car. This needs a car or shuttle at the Snow Lakes trailhead; reversing Aasgard Pass is the alternative.

days.objective: Descend past Viviane, Snow and Nada lakes

days.note: Walk or bike the 8 closed miles of Suiattle River Road from the milepost 12 gate to the Downey Creek trailhead first. Hike the mostly gentle Downey Creek Trail to Sixmile Camp, then continue up the abandoned, brushy Bachelor Creek Trail to a flat camp near 4,500 ft. Expect slide-alder bushwhacking and a footlog crossing of Bachelor Creek; parties report this day taking most of a full day with full packs.
days.title: Approach to Bachelor Creek
days.objective: Reach forest camp near the Bachelor Creek crossing (Sixmile Camp / Bachelor Flats)

days.note: Climb steep forest and meadow above Bachelor Flats, cross the snow slopes of Cub Lake Pass (~5,700 ft), and drop to Cub Lake or climb onto Itswoot Ridge to camp with views of the Dome/Chickamin Glacier. This is normally the crux navigation day if snow-covered.
days.title: Over Cub Lake Pass to high camp
days.objective: Establish high camp on Itswoot Ridge or in the Cub Lake basin

days.note: An alpine-start glacier day: rope up and cross the Chickamin Glacier to the Dome-Sinister col, then climb the loose southwest gully and scramble the upper west ridge (Class 2-3) to the summit. Reverse the same line back to camp; parties reach the summit anywhere from late morning to early afternoon depending on party speed and whether Dome Peak is tagged the same day.
days.title: Climb Sinister Peak

schedule.label: Top out on the upper west ridge

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the gully and glacier crossing.

days.objective: Summit via the Southwest Route and return to high camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the full approach in one long push: back over Cub Lake Pass, down Bachelor Creek, and out the Downey Creek Trail, then the 8 closed miles of road to the milepost 12 gate. Most parties treat this as a single long descent day rather than splitting it again.
